/itineraryStops/7/description.source_en:
**⟦G0⟧ (감천문화마을)** — nicknamed both **'Korea's Machu Picchu'** and **'Korea's Santorini'** — is a hillside neighborhood in Saha-gu, west Busan, whose pastel-painted houses cascade down in stepped rows over the slope. 

The settlement began in the **1920s–1930s** when the Busan administration relocated working-class residents away from the port. The village's character was set in **1955** when **~800 families (about 4,000 people) of the Taegeukdo religious community** — a uniquely Korean syncretic religion blending Buddhist, Confucian, and yin-yang elements, founded by **Jo Cheol-je** during the Japanese colonial period — settled here as Korean War refugees fleeing the North. 

The Taegeukdo philosophy of '**allowing others to prosper**' directly shaped the village's most distinctive feature: houses are intentionally tiered so that **no roof blocks the view of the house behind it**, with the entire community visible to the sky and the sea. Gamcheon remained one of Busan's poorest neighborhoods until **2009**, when the Korean Ministry of Culture launched the **'Dreaming of Machu Picchu in Busan'** public-art revitalization project, followed by the **'Miro Miro' (maze) project in 2010** — adding 22+ commissioned murals, sculptures, and art installations including the iconic **'Little Prince and Fox' bench** at the Sky Garden viewpoint. 

Gamcheon won the **2012 UN-HABITAT Asian Townscape Award** and now welcomes **~1.4 million visitors annually**. The visit follows the village's signature stamp-map walking route: from the entrance at the **Tourist Information Center**, up to **Sky Garden viewpoint** for the panoramic rainbow-roof shot, then down through the labyrinthine alleys past murals, hanbok rental shops, craft workshops, and small cafes. 

**The village is a living residential community** — quiet voices required, no drones, no flash photography into homes, and rubbish carried out. 

Hours **09:00–18:00 Mar–Oct / 09:00–17:00 Nov–Feb (info center)**; **village itself open 24h, FREE entry**.

/itineraryStops/7/visitBasics/hours.source_en: Daily 09:00–18:00 (Mar–Oct) / 09:00–17:00 (Nov–Feb); some shops/cafes keep their own hours

/itineraryStops/7/visitBasics/walking.source_en: Strenuous — very steep alleys and stairs; not stroller- or wheelchair-friendly in many sections

/itineraryStops/7/visitBasics/admission.source_en: Free village entry; optional Stamp Map ≈ 2,000 KRW

/itineraryStops/8/timeUsed/0.source_en: Coach drop-off at Songdo Marine Park (~5 min)

/itineraryStops/8/timeUsed/2.source_en: Beach promenade + Songdo Marine Cable Car viewing (no ride included) (~10 min)

/itineraryStops/8/highlights/0.source_en: **Korea's FIRST modern public beach** — opened **1913** during the Japanese colonial era

/itineraryStops/8/highlights/1.source_en: **800 m long × 50 m wide** crescent of fine sand on Busan's southwest coast (Seo-gu)

/itineraryStops/8/highlights/2.source_en: **Songdo Marine Cable Car (송도해상케이블카)** — 1.62 km roundtrip over the bay; **reopened June 2017** after a 1988 closure; **86 m max altitude**; **'Crystal cabin' option** with glass floor

/itineraryStops/8/highlights/3.source_en: **Songdo Cloud Trails (송도구름산책로)** — 365 m curved skywalk over the sea, opened 2016, replaces the older Songdo Skywalk

/itineraryStops/8/highlights/4.source_en: **Songdo Yonggungungu Suspension Bridge** — connecting the beach park to nearby Amnam Park

/itineraryStops/8/highlights/5.source_en: Annual **⟦G0⟧ Festival** (June–August) with sand sculpture contest and night markets

/itineraryStops/8/highlights/6.source_en: **Free beach access 24h**; cable car ₩17,000 round-trip adult (own expense, not included)

/itineraryStops/8/smartNotes/tip.source_en: The Songdo Marine Cable Car is **NOT included** in this bus tour and the 30-minute stop is too short to ride it (a full round-trip with queue is ~45–60 min); guests who want to ride should choose our private cruise-shore charter instead; the Cloud Trails skywalk is free and reachable within the 30-min window

/itineraryStops/8/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Public restrooms at Songdo Marine Park visitor center; convenience stores along Songdohaebyeon-ro; the cable-car lower station has a cafe and Korean War Memorial exhibit

/itineraryStops/8/whyOnRoute.source_en: ⟦G1⟧ is the route's **late-afternoon coastal reset** — after the dense Nampo-dong urban cluster (Jagalchi + BIFF + Gukje + Gamcheon's hillside), a short stop at Korea's oldest public beach gives cruise guests a final breath of sea air before the day's ⟦G0⟧ / cruise-terminal close. The 17:45 timing lands at **late golden hour**, the most photogenic light for the cable-car-over-water shot. The 30-min stop is intentionally short — enough for the Cloud Trails skywalk and a few coastline photos, but not enough for a cable-car ride (which is treated as a separate paid experience for guests on longer Busan trips).

/itineraryStops/8/convenience/parking.source_en: Songdo Marine Park public lot, coach-accessible

/itineraryStops/8/convenience/restroom.source_en: Songdo Marine Park visitor center and convenience stores along Songdohaebyeon-ro
